item.title: Caitlin Clark's record-breaking August sets the stage for her FIBA Women's World Cup debut
item.description: Caitlin Clark set multiple WNBA records in August, scoring or assisting on 44.7 points per game and more before her FIBA Women's World Cup debut.
item.content:encoded:
Caitlin Clark is gearing up for her first appearance in the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup on Friday, and if she plays like she did for the Indiana Fever this past month, Team USA may be impossible to take down.

Clark’s August in the WNBA was a spectacle to behold, as she once again made league history with her phenomenal play.

For starters, Clark scored or assisted on 44.7 points per game, a WNBA record for a single month. The stellar point guard has always had a knack for either finding the bottom of the net or dishing assists to her teammates to get the job done.

CAITLIN CLARK, INDIANA FEVER GO INTO FIBA WORLD CUP BREAK WITH BIG WIN OVER CONNECTICUT

Either way, those numbers were racked up throughout the month of August, and more history followed.

Clark became the first player in WNBA history with back-to-back 30-plus-point and 10-plus-assist games.

They both came in the final two games for the Fever before this international break, scoring 34 points with 12 assists in a 111-91 win over the Connecticut Sun. Then, Clark poured in 37 points, including eight of 12 three-pointers made, with 10 assists in the Aug. 23 win over the Chicago Sky, 113-90.

That game against the Sky was also significant, as Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from the Wintrust Arena in Chicago after an altercation involving Sky guard Natasha Cloud. The third-quarter incident, though, never rattled Clark and the Fever, and they got the job done before heading back home.

USA WOMEN'S BASKETBALL ROSTER REVEAL FOR FIBA WORLD CUP FEATURES AWKWARD CAITLIN CLARK, ANGEL REESE PAIRING

It's also worth mentioning the off-the-court situation that made national headlines involving Freedom considering the Fever's caption called Clark's performance "HERstoric." Kanter, fellow Fever star Sophie Cunningham, and many others have spoken out about their belief that biological men should be out of women's sports.

Meanwhile, a WNBA task force of team presidents and general managers met last month to discuss a wide range of topics, one of which being transgender athletes. However, they did not arrive at any eligibility rules, which basically means the league can't define what a woman is.

"Today's meeting covered a wide range of topics, including ongoing discussions on transgender athletes and the continued hate and vitriol directed at players online," the WNBA’s statement read. "We will continue to engage all league stakeholders in the coming weeks and months. We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league. There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others."

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT SENDS TRANS INCLUSION MEMO AFTER ENES FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE ANNOUNCEMENTS

So, while play on words does make sense here with "HERstoric," it falls a bit flat considering what's been happening off the court with the WNBA. But there's no doubting the history that Clark continues to make.

Clark put together five games in August where she had at least 20 points and 10 assists. To put that into perspective, no other player had five such games in the last five seasons combined.

Finally, Clark averaged 24.4 points per game, which was the highest-scoring month by a point guard in WNBA history.

The Fever went 7-4 in their August stretch, bringing them to 26-14 on the season thus far. That record is good for fifth in the WNBA standings, though it is quite tight between those in front, and behind, Indiana.

The Fever have only four games remaining in their regular-season schedule once they return from the international break. Clark and the rest of her teammates will be sure to hit the ground running and try to get hot heading into the playoffs.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy jury wraps day 6 with bombshell one-juror standoff, deliberations to resume Friday
item.description: Lindsay Clancy’s jury ended its sixth day without a verdict after a dispute involving a holdout juror, with deliberations set to resume Friday.
item.content:encoded:
The jury deciding Lindsay Clancy’s fate ended a dramatic sixth day of deliberations Thursday without a verdict amid a dispute involving a holdout juror, with deliberations set to resume Friday.

The panel of nine women and three men has twice reported being deadlocked. Jurors are expected to return Friday, when Judge William Sullivan is also set to address a dispute involving one member of the panel.

Earlier Thursday, defense attorney Kevin Reddington unsuccessfully sought to remove a juror after the foreperson reported that the person was refusing to follow the court’s instructions on reasonable doubt.

Reddington warned that the case could end without a verdict because of a juror who had "spurned the instructions" of the court.

LINDSAY CLANCY JURY RECAP: DAY 5 ENDS WITH NO VERDICT AFTER RARE INSTRUCTION

Prosecutors objected to removing anyone, arguing there was no way to determine who was right or wrong without improperly examining the jury’s private deliberations. They said Sullivan had acted appropriately by questioning the jurors about whether they could follow the law and again instructing them on reasonable doubt.

WHAT IS A TUEY-RODRIGUEZ CHARGE? JUDGE GIVES INSTRUCTION TO DEADLOCKED LINDSAY CLANCY JURY

Sullivan declined, calling the removal of a deliberating juror "a sensitive undertaking" and saying the court could not take sides in the jury’s deliberations.

After court, Reddington revealed that a later jury note appeared to show an 11-to-1 divide.

SOCIAL MEDIA IS LINDSAY CLANCY WILD CARD THAT COULD TILT POTENTIAL RETRIAL TO THE DEFENSE, RETIRED JUDGE SAYS

"When a note that the judge already has says that there are 11 jurors that have made a decision and one juror will not apply reasonable [doubt]..." Reddington said.

The note does not reveal which verdict the 11 jurors favor or how the remaining juror is leaning.

HARVEY WEINSTEIN RAPE TRIAL ENDS IN MISTRIAL AFTER JURY DEADLOCKED

Reddington said Sullivan plans to hold an inquiry at 9 a.m. Friday. If jurors again say they cannot reach a unanimous decision, the case could end in a mistrial.

The defense attorney said he expects the arguments over the jury issue to take place in open court rather than at sidebar.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S FUTURE COULD REST WITH ‘PROSECUTION DOCTORS’ AS CASE ECHOES INFAMOUS MAINE KILLINGS: EXPERT

Asked whether a retrial could favor prosecutors, Reddington issued a blunt response.

"Bring it," he said, adding that his witnesses and evidence are ready.

"I got witnesses lined up. We’re all set. Dr. Resnick is ready. I’m ready. We’ve got all our evidence. Witnesses are available, so let’s go," Reddington said.

Reddington said prosecutors might seek to put off another trial "for six months or a year," but indicated he would be ready to move quickly. He deferred to Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz when questioned about the possibility of a plea agreement.

"Let’s see what Mr. Cruz wants to do, and then we’ll talk about our options," Reddington said.

Clancy, 36, faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children, Cora, Dawson and Callan, who were all under the age of 6 when they were found strangled in the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023.

LINDSAY CLANCY VERDICT: RETIRED JUDGE EXPLAINS WHAT HAPPENS IF INSANITY DEFENSE PREVAILS

She does not dispute killing them. Jurors must instead decide whether she was criminally responsible at the time.

Prosecutors argue Clancy understood what she was doing and should be held responsible for the children’s deaths. Her attorneys contend she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and could not appreciate the wrongfulness of her actions or conform her conduct to the law.

The jury is considering several possible outcomes, including first-degree murder, second-degree murder, voluntary or involuntary manslaughter, not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility, or not guilty.

item.title: WATCH: Bystanders, police lift Volkswagen off woman pinned underneath after dramatic e-bike crash
item.description: Body camera video captured strangers and officers lifting a Volkswagen Beetle off a trapped e-bike rider after a crash on a Prospect Park road.
item.content:encoded:
A group of strangers and police officers rushed to lift a Volkswagen Beetle off an injured e-bike rider after she became trapped beneath the car during a crash on a busy Pennsylvania road, dramatic body camera video shows.

Local authorities said the 44-year-old woman suffered several broken bones in Monday morning's crash in Prospect Park but survived after roughly six bystanders joined officers to lift the vehicle and pull her to safety, FOX 29 reported.

Prospect Park Police Chief Dave Madonna said the woman was riding an e-bike more than 20 mph, according to his estimate, without a helmet when she collided with the Volkswagen at an intersection along Route 420.

"She was driving way too fast for that time of day, for the road she was traveling on," Madonna said, adding that he believed she had been trying to overtake vehicles while traveling to an appointment.

RESCUERS FREE CLIMBER TRAPPED BENEATH 16,000-POUND BOULDER ON OREGON'S MOUNT HOOD IN COMPLEX OPERATION

Surveillance and police body camera video shows bystanders rushing to the crash to help.

About six people then work together to lift the car high enough to free the woman trapped underneath.

"Got a yell to help, ran over. We lifted the Volkswagen Beetle up, pulled the girl out and pushed her to the ground so she wouldn't move, that's all," FedEx driver Carl Wise told the station.

GOOD SAMARITAN IN SPIDER-MAN COSTUME HELPS MAN IN WHEELCHAIR CROSS BUSY INTERSECTION IN VIRAL MOMENT

"I'm no hero. I'm just a guy doing a job, that's all," he added.

Local business owner Chrissy Vollmer, who also responded, described what she saw.

"All I saw were the lady's legs underneath the car, and she was just yelling, ‘Get this car off of me,’" Vollmer said.

Madonna called the bystanders who helped rescue the woman "heroes" and later visited them to offer his thanks.

ICE OFFICER HAILED AS HERO AFTER SAVING DRIVER INJURED IN MISSOURI CRASH

He also raised concerns about what he described as an increase in e-bike crashes.

"How many more tragedies do we have to see before some type of action is taken?" Madonna said.

The woman was taken to Lankenau Hospital and underwent surgery for a broken collarbone and other injuries, FOX 29 reported.

The Volkswagen driver is not facing charges, and  police said the e-bike rider could receive a traffic citation pending the outcome of the investigation.

item.title: Missouri high court blocks GOP-backed congressional maps ahead of midterms; Trump blasts 'ridiculous' ruling
item.description: The Missouri Supreme Court unanimously blocked the GOP-drawn map, and President Donald Trump called the ruling "ridiculous" before November's vote.
item.content:encoded:
The Missouri Supreme Court on Thursday unanimously blocked newly enacted Republican-backed congressional districts from being used in November's midterm elections, ruling that voters must first approve the map in a statewide referendum.

The ruling marks a rare setback for Republicans in a national redistricting battle. 

The GOP had aimed to use Missouri’s new congressional map to help them win an additional seat and hold onto its slim House majority.

The court ruled that the referendum petition, filed in December after opponents submitted more than 300,000 signatures, prevented the new districts from taking effect unless approved by voters. 

DEMS DERIDED TRUMP'S MIDTERM GAMBLE — UNTIL HE ENDED UP WINNING BIG

Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins waited until primary Election Day last month to reject the petition, arguing that the referendum process cannot be used for congressional redistricting. A lower court sided with Hoskins, but the state Supreme Court overturned his decision.

"The referendum petition was legal, sufficient, and timely, and the secretary incorrectly concluded otherwise," the court said in its ruling. The measure with the new districts "did not go into effect and will not go into effect unless and until approved by the voters."

Now, the congressional map adopted after the 2020 census "remains in full force and effect for the November 2026 general election," the court said.

Once considered a swing state, Missouri has dramatically shifted to the right over the past two decades.

Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, a Republican, plans to immediately appeal the case to the U.S. Supreme Court.

"Never before in American history has a court overturned a congressional map after a primary and before a general election. This unprecedented decision clearly violates federal law and has thrust our state into a full‑fledged constitutional crisis," Hanaway said in a statement. 

"We are confident that the federal courts will not allow every Missouri voter to be disenfranchised, which is what today’s decision does."

President Donald Trump called Thursday's ruling "ridiculous" and argued it was unconstitutional, saying there will not be enough time to change the map before November's elections.

"The Missouri Supreme Court just ridiculously ruled in favor of changing the maps back to what they were a long time ago," he wrote on Truth Social. "It’s called, Ancient History! The problem is, according to Legal Scholars, that not only was the ruling horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional, but there won’t be enough time to change the map back with the Election coming up in a very short period of time. 

"The Election Process, as usual, is being disturbed in America! Missouri must be able to use the map that was in effect just a couple of months ago, in the Primary. This is a Dark Day for 'Justice' in Missouri!"

Missouri’s new districts were used in the primaries last month, but the state Supreme Court said they cannot be used again unless voters first uphold the new districts passed by the GOP-controlled legislature and signed by Republican Gov. Mike Kehoe last September.

Kehoe said he is "extremely disappointed in today’s decision by unelected judges and their lack of respect for the legislative process."

"Holding a primary election under one congressional map and a general election under another is unprecedented and creates uncertainty for Missouri voters," he said on X. "Today’s ruling does not change our belief in the Missouri First Map or the principles behind it, and we will continue to stand behind it as the legal process moves forward."

Five of the seven current justices on the Missouri Supreme Court, including the chief justice, were appointed by Republican governors.

The new map targeted longtime Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver's Kansas City-area district by shifting it eastward to include rural right-leaning voters. The map was intended to make Cleaver's district more favorable to Republicans, who hoped it would produce a 7-1 advantage in the state's congressional delegation.

SUPREME COURT ALLOWS ALABAMA GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAP FOR MIDTERMS

Cleaver responded to the ruling by saying, "The people fought back and won."

"More than 305,000 Missourians demanded a say in who will represent them in the halls of Congress," he wrote on X. "Despite the cynical and deeply shameful attempt to silence many of our neighbors, the people fought back and won. This reaffirms that the people should choose their politicians, not the other way around. Democracy prevails."

Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin also called it a "big win for democracy and the people of Missouri."

"Democrats will continue fighting to end the Republican gerrymandering sham and ensure all voters can make their voices heard," he wrote on X.

Fox News' Paul Steinhauser and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Here's why, even with all its problems, college football is still better than the NFL
item.description: The College Football Playoff's tight 12-team field means week one upsets can derail entire seasons, a pressure the NFL's 14-team format never matches.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a tough offseason for college football, with discussions on expanding the College Football Playoff, Lane Kiffin's NFL-to-LSU pipeline, and the ever-expanding crisis of tampering and abuses in the transfer portal or in NIL.

While week zero has already come and gone, college football is officially and fully back for week one, starting Thursday evening and continuing without the long Labor Day weekend. And it's a reminder of the many reasons why there's so much more to like and enjoy in the collegiate ranks compared to its big NFL brother.

Here's just a few of them.

WEEK ONE UPSET SPECIAL: THESE THREE COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS SHOULD BE ON UPSET ALERT THIS WEEKEND

It's the first full week of the season, but with the number of teams in major conferences and the limited spots in the College Football Playoff, each game means something for many programs. A whopping 14 teams reach the postseason in the NFL, out of 32, meaning an incredible 44% of the league makes the playoff.

In the NCAA, there are 68 teams between the Big Ten, SEC, ACC, Big 12 and Notre Dame. Just 12 teams reach the College Football Playoff, and one of those spots automatically goes to a Group of 6 team. Not every program in those conferences has realistic hopes of reaching the playoff, but with just 11 spots to go around, just 16.1% of those top teams can play meaningful postseason football.

In the 2025 NFL season, for example, the 9-7-1 Green Bay Packers and 8-9 Carolina Panthers made the postseason. Depending on the division or strength of your conference, teams that finish around .500 have a realistic possibility of making the playoffs. Yes, the games "matter," but a loss in week one of the NFL season carries little weight or meaning.

In college? It matters. The expanded playoff gives teams room for one or two losses, potentially three this year, depending on schedule, but one slip up in week one can remove any margin for error. Notre Dame in 2025, for example, lost their first game of the season to an eventual playoff team in Miami, lost in week two to another playoff team, Texas A&M, and were left out of the 12-team field.

CLEMSON'S DABO SWINNEY THROWS SHADE AT LANE KIFFIN, LSU OVER BRINGING IN NFL PLAYERS: 'IT'S EMBARRASSING'

LSU and Clemson both have realistic hopes of reaching the playoffs. And while the loser of Saturday's game isn't eliminated, the path gets harder. Clemson, given their fairly weak schedule, has to beat Miami when the two play next month. LSU plays Ole Miss, Texas A&M, Alabama, Texas, and Tennessee. An early season slip up makes finishing their season with two losses nearly impossible.

That's another element to it, upsets matter. Because of the importance of subjective rankings, not objective standings. The Los Angeles Rams are widely expected to be the best team in the NFL this year. If they lose to the New York Giants at home in week two, it doesn't matter more than any other loss in the regular season. Division tiebreakers notwithstanding.

ESPN PUTS 20TH RANKED TENNESSEE ON UPSET ALERT, AND YOU'LL NEVER GUESS WHO THEY'RE PLAYING

But if Wisconsin beats Notre Dame on Sunday? That changes the season. As unlikely as that outcome is, it's not impossible. Which, once again, makes college football more exciting.

There's no doubt that the NFL offers a higher level of quality football. The players are more athletic, physical, faster, and more developed. Coaching is generally better than at the collegiate level. And the draft ensures that only the best of the best reach NFL training camps and rosters.

But therein lies some of the problems. Defenses, in particular, are just too good.

The NFL has tried to mitigate some of this obvious disconnect with several rule changes. The new kickoffs have moved field position further up than in years past. Then they started allowing teams to manipulate the actual football that kickers use, the K-ball, allowing them to make increasingly lengthy field goals. With 65–70 yards now a realistic possibility, offenses in the NFL could be in field goal range after picking up just 15–20 yards after a touch back. These changes were clearly made with scoring in mind, because year after year, the offense keeps declining.

Those aren't the only rules; the laughable overprotection of quarterbacks was done to ensure that the league's stars stayed healthy and prevent backups from the 6-21 for 76-yard stat line that they're known for. Increasing the focus on illegal contact penalties was also done to give offenses more advantages.

While there are a handful of games each year in the NFL that are chaotic and exciting, they're few and far between compared to college. Why? Because college players aren't as good.

It's easier to move the ball. Higher scoring games are common. There are dozens of wild, unpredictable comebacks throughout the collegiate ranks. "Pac-12 after dark" became a running joke on social media, before that conference's demise, but the sentiment lives on.

Particularly in one specific type of match-up.

Yes, the NFL has rivalries, games like Cowboys-Commanders, Packers-Bears, or Chargers-Raiders that have elevated meaning for the fans of both teams. But the importance of those games pales in comparison to traditional college football rivalries.

Texas-Oklahoma. USC—UCLA or USC—Notre Dame. Alabama—Auburn. Michigan—Ohio State. Army—Navy. Florida—Georgia. Oregon—Oregon State. Texas—Texas A&M. Florida—Florida State. Utah—BYU. Cal—Stanford. There are many, many more.

While it's probably an overstatement to say that a disappointing season can be undone just by beating your rival, but it's not far off. And obviously far exceeds the importance placed on rivalry games in the NFL, playoffs aside. Nobody's getting fired in the NFL based on their record against rivals alone, but an Ohio State coach that can't beat Michigan? Or vice versa? That almost immediately puts them on the hot seat.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The NFL has perfected the bland luxury box. The "glass box house" style of stadium building. There are exceptions, of course, like Lambeau Field, Arrowhead, and Lumen Field in Seattle, but is anyone falling over themselves to make a pilgrimage to Mercedes-Benz Stadium? Or MetLife? Or Levi's Stadium?

College football teams, meanwhile, play games at the Rose Bowl. The Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Tiger Stadium in Louisiana. Beaver Stadium. Notre Dame Stadium. Washington's home stadium, literally on Lake Washington. Colorado plays its home games at the base of the Rockies. There are incredible atmospheres at places like Kyle Field, Autzen Stadium, Lane Field, Memorial Stadium in Nebraska, Sanford Stadium, Doak Campbell, "The Swamp," tailgating in The Grove. BYU, Utah, DKR, Appalachian State.

There are iconic venues across the country, each with their own traditions, unique settings, and experiences. The NFL just can't compete, because the primary objective is ensuring that corporate sponsors have places for people to network while "watching" a game.

College football season is here, the sport's fans should remember how important it is not to take it for granted. The alternative is watching the NFL.

item.title: Michael Lombardi leaves North Carolina football GM role, university's internal probe continues
item.description: Michael Lombardi resigned as UNC football's highest-paid college GM amid an ongoing internal investigation, weeks into Bill Belichick's second season.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Lombardi will no longer be part of the North Carolina football program. The longtime NFL executive stepped down Thursday from his most recent role as the college program’s general manager, UNC announced Thursday.

Lombardi’s decision comes more than a month after the university placed him on paid administrative leave amid an internal investigation. Even with Lombardi’s resignation, the probe launched by UNC’s Office of University Counsel will proceed, the school confirmed.

Lombardi arrived at Chapel Hill in 2025, ahead of Bill Belichick’s first season, and was widely considered one of the seven-time Super Bowl-winning coach’s most trusted advisors within the football program.

UNC GM MICHAEL LOMBARDI CLAIMS 'FAKE STORIES' HELPED UNDERMINE BILL BELICHICK’S DEBUT SEASON

"Effective September 3, 2026, Michael Lombardi has resigned from his position as General Manager of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill’s football program," the university said Thursday in a press release sent to Fox News Digital.

"The University will continue its ongoing investigation and will consider all appropriate corrective actions responsive to the information it learns."

The internal investigation into Lombardi became public in late July. At the time, the Office of University Counsel cited unspecified allegations and said it would not comment on their nature.

"Because this involves confidential personnel issues, the University will not comment on the nature of the allegations or discuss personnel Information," a statement issued on July 28 read.

After North Carolina named Lombardi general manager, he became college football’s highest-paid football operations executive, earning an annual salary of $1.5 million. Lombardi was among Belichick’s first hires after he accepted the job at UNC.

Belichick reacted to Lombardi being placed on administrative leave on July 30.

"Well, we’re working through some things," Belichick told reporters as the Tar Heels opened preseason camp. "We’re at a particular time of year now where there are some things in play and some things that aren’t in play that won’t happen until later in the calendar year. Again, we’re taking it day-to-day, and we’re doing things that are on Day 1. … We’ve made a few adjustments, but we’re working through the process."

Belichick’s second season at North Carolina got off to a promising start when the Tar Heels upset TCU in Ireland last Saturday. UNC finished Belichick’s debut season with a 4-8 record.

item.title: Judge grants injunction against NCAA, SEC, allowing athletes with NFL ties eligible to play for LSU, others
item.description: A Louisiana judge granted an injunction on Thursday to allow athletes with professional ties to play for LSU and others to start a wild week in college football.
item.content:encoded:
The scene outside a district court just miles away from LSU's campus was the epicenter of college athletics, as the NCAA and SEC appeared in court to argue their case against athletes with NFL ties returning to college athletics.

A sea of reporters swarmed Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill as she exited her vehicle, opening her short media scrum with a "Go Tigers," which set the scene for what was a wild day inside the 19th District Court.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

At the forefront of this case, with LSU head coach Lane Kiffin emphasizing multiple times that the Tigers were just obeying a court order that was previously issued allowing the school to roster athletes like former Cleveland Browns training camp tight end Dae'Quan Wright, was the argument that players with NFL or professional ties should not be allowed back in college athletics.

What started in one state court has now spread across the country, with a plethora of athletes filing lawsuits against the NCAA, and now SEC, over new guidelines enacted pertaining to the five-for-five eligibility.

Inside the Baton Rouge courtroom, lawyers for the plaintiffs, NCAA and SEC argued over whether these athletes should be granted a temporary injunction.

In the end, Judge William Jorden ruled in the favor of athletes, granting them an injunction that will allow them to be rostered this upcoming season by any school that will take them.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

A day that felt more like a John Grisham novel unfolding in real-time had lawyers from all sides arguing over what is right and what is actually legal.

There was the testimony of SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey, who was on the stand for over three hours, being peppered with questions from plaintiff attorneys about how the conference can allow professional athletes who have played overseas be granted the ability to play over five seasons, compared to these plaintiffs who turned pro under the previous guidelines that left them without eligibility.

Three minutes after Sankey took the stand, the SEC filed a federal lawsuit in Alabama against LSU and Kiffin, accusing them of orchestrating the recruitment of multiple athletes who would then go on to sue the conference in a Louisiana court.

This sent shockwaves through the courtroom, after plaintiff attorney Tony Clayton asked three different times whether the SEC had filed a lawsuit this morning in Alabama. It played out in real time, as lawyers for the plaintiffs were checking their phones after notifications started going off that showed the SEC had filed their suit in federal court.

Call it gamesmanship, or the SEC trying to distract from what was transpiring in Baton Rouge, but it turned out to be one of the crazier things we've seen in these eligibility lawsuits.

The following three hours were both entertainment and the plaintiffs trying to prove that the SEC colluded to enact new guidelines pertaining to former pro-athletes returning to college in the days after the initial court order was issued in this same court.

This part was an aspect of the case that Judge William Jorden could not get past.

item.title: Officials identify victims killed, officers injured in Minneapolis apartment shooting
item.description: Minnesota officials identified the two civilians killed and the Minneapolis police officers injured during Wednesday’s deadly apartment shooting.
item.content:encoded:
Minnesota officials released the identities of the victims involved in Wednesday’s Minneapolis apartment shooting that left two civilians dead and two police officers injured by gunfire.

The two civilians were Dale Henry Spry, 63, and Muse A. Afrah, 61, according to the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension (BCA). Officials previously said one victim died at the apartment complex and the other died at a hospital.

Both victims are believed to have been residents of the apartment complex where Carlton Neal Johnson II, 35, opened fire before he was fatally struck in an exchange of gunfire with police. A preliminary autopsy indicated Johnson died after sustaining multiple gunshot wounds, and his death was ruled a homicide, officials said.

The two Minneapolis Police Department (MPD) officers injured in the shooting were identified as Joseph Michnowski, a five-year veteran, and Yahye Ahmed, a nearly two-year veteran, according to the BCA.

3 DEAD, INCLUDING SUSPECTED GUNMAN, AND 3 OFFICERS INJURED IN MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING

Ahmed was released from a hospital Thursday, while Michnowski remained hospitalized Thursday afternoon, interim Police Chief Bill Peterson said during a briefing.

Garrett Parten, an MPD public information officer, said one of the injured officers sustained an apparent non-life-threatening gunshot wound to the leg, while the other underwent surgery.

Another officer involved in the incident was also evaluated for an apparent non-life-threatening injury, Parten said.

MINNEAPOLIS APARTMENT SHOOTING SUSPECT WAS FACING EVICTION: REPORT

Peterson identified the third officer as Ernest Boateng but clarified that his injuries were not directly related to the gunfire. Boateng was cut by glass while breaking a window of a locked police vehicle whose sirens were going off, Peterson said.

Boateng was evaluated and released Wednesday.

The BCA said at least one officer discharged his gun during the incident, identifying the officer as Liban Mohamed Ibrahim, a two-year MPD veteran.

"Investigators are continuing to determine whether any other officers fired their weapons," BCA said.

Wednesday’s shooting began during a domestic child custody exchange involving a woman who previously had a relationship with Johnson, according to Drew Evans, superintendent of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension.

Johnson reportedly shot the woman outside the building before going inside the apartment, where he shot another facility worker. He then went to the ninth floor, where he shot two residents who later died.

He was also facing eviction from the apartment building, according to court records obtained by Fox9 Minneapolis.

Officials have not determined whether Johnson specifically targeted the victims.

item.title: New HBO superhero show faces 'woke' criticism for reframing classic hero lore around racial privilege
item.description: HBO's "Lanterns" reframes John Stewart's Green Lantern origin through racial politics, sparking accusations that Damon Lindelof's series went "woke."
item.content:encoded:
HBO’s new superhero series, "Lanterns," drew criticism from some viewers who accused the studio of overhauling a beloved character’s origin story to focus on modern racial discourse and privilege.

Episode 3, "OutKast," reframes the franchise's traditional emphasis on "fearlessness" through the experience of a Black man in America, prompting some critics to accuse the show of sacrificing classic comic book lore for social justice commentary.

In DC Comics lore, Green Lanterns are intergalactic peacekeepers chosen by alien power rings that seek out individuals with the innate ability to overcome fear. In "Lanterns," that standard is reframed as an unfair burden when applied to Stewart.

BELOVED 'LITTLE HOUSE ON THE PRAIRIE' FACES WAGONLOAD OF 'WOKE' ALLEGATIONS OVER NETFLIX REBOOT

"Do you know the differences in race on Earth?" Stewart's mother, Bernadette, asks an alien Guardian of the Universe who has taken the form of an older White woman. "Do you understand how unfair it is to ask a Black man in America if he’s afraid?

"We are terrified daily of persecution and still show up, sometimes better than everyone around us," Bernadette adds. "Even in space, y’all don’t consider us."

Rather than being chosen as an adult for his ability to overcome fear, Stewart is conditioned by his parents from infancy in "Lanterns" to wield the ring through hyper-precise perfection. Some viewers accused the show of replacing the hero’s traditional emphasis on individual willpower with a lesson on racial privilege.

"Lanterns" co-creator Damon Lindelof also created HBO’s 2019 superhero series "Watchmen," which similarly drew criticism over its focus on American racial politics. 

But not everyone online objected to the changes.

'THE BOYS' CREATOR ADMITS 'SINKING FEELING' AS REALITY 'OUT-CRAZIES' HIS POLITICAL FINAL SEASON

"Lanterns is fantastic. And for those inevitably crying that they ruined GL by going ‘woke,’ you obviously never read O’Neil & Adams’ Green Lantern/Green Arrow run," filmmaker and comic book writer Steven DeKnight, who previously worked on "Daredevil," wrote on X.

The character John Stewart debuted in 1971 as one of DC’s first Black superheroes. He was portrayed as a civil rights advocate who challenged authorities in Detroit and as a fearless leader whose willpower earned him the Green Lantern ring.

Critics argue that "Lanterns" alters that characterization by making Stewart’s childhood conditioning, rather than his natural willpower, central to his selection.

"Lanterns" writer and co-executive producer Vanessa Baden Kelly addressed the character’s comic origins and accusations that the show had gone "woke" in an interview with TheWrap.

ISSA RAE SAYS DEI HAS BECOME A 'BAD WORD' IN HOLLYWOOD AS EXECUTIVES OF COLOR 'TIPTOE' TO KEEP JOBS

"I stumbled across some people calling the show ‘woke,’ and there were people putting panels in the reactions and the comments, and they were panels from the 1970s John Stewart," Baden Kelly said.

"Him calling people ‘Whitey’ or him opposing wars, and I’m like, ‘Oh my God.’ I read a bunch, but I couldn’t read all of it, and you’re just like, that’s right, just keep it in the front of your mind — that this is who John Stewart’s always been," she added.

In the same article, J. Alphonse Nicholson, who plays the hero's father, John Stewart Sr., in flashbacks, discussed the show’s portrayal of racial dynamics.

"I’m just grateful that the writing room put this into the script," Nicholson told TheWrap. "How can you expect this African American man in this world … to be fearless? It really raises a lot of questions on who has the privilege to move through life without thinking about those things, even in the fictional world."

Nicholson also linked the show to the 2024 presidential election during an appearance on pop culture creator Fantastic Frankey’s podcast, arguing the country is experiencing the consequences of "not trusting a Black woman."

"Could you imagine where we would be right now if Kamala got up in there, dog? Could you imagine how we would’ve been? It’d be a lot different, right? So we’re experiencing the consequences of not trusting a Black woman," Nicholson said in the clip, connecting the show’s themes of heroism to Harris’ 2024 candidacy.

KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS IT'S 'EXHAUSTING' WHEN MOVIES TRY TO ALTER HISTORY TO FIT MODERN TASTES

"And now we have this show in a way that can [kind of] tell you how great it could be. How great of a superhero we can create and have if you trust a Black woman."

Entertainment critic Christian Toto argued the creative choices in "Lanterns" reflect a broader trend in modern-day entertainment.

"Today's Hollywood screenwriters care little about canon or fidelity to the source material," Christian Toto, host of "The Hollywood in Toto Podcast," told Fox News Digital. "They love injecting modern culture war battles into storylines, even when they don't mesh with the material or present themselves as awkward and unnecessary."

Toto argued that the show’s dialogue risks alienating audiences despite what he described as "strong ratings."

"That's precisely what's happening with the show so far. Make no mistake. This is overtly woke in nature. The scribes are jamming social justice arguments into the dialogue in ways that feel inauthentic to the time period in question. Even worse? The on-the-nose dialogue takes us out of the story," Toto said.

"The pushback was inevitable. Audiences sense this kind of clunky woke storytelling a mile away. And many are exhausted by it. Yet the series is getting strong ratings to date, so general audiences are so interested in the comic book characters they'll often look past the woke detours. At least for now."

Fox News Digital reached out to Warner Bros. Discovery but did not immediately hear back.

item.title: Trump names Adam Telle acting secretary of the Army following Dan Driscoll's resignation
item.description: Adam Telle steps in as acting Army secretary after Dan Driscoll's resignation amid reported clashes with Pete Hegseth over Army readiness efforts.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Thursday announced he was appointing Adam Telle, assistant secretary of the Army for Civil Works, as acting secretary of the Army.

"I am pleased to announce that Adam Telle, the current Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works, will become Acting Secretary of the Army, effective immediately," Trump posted on Truth Social.

"He is a Great Patriot, who is respected by all."

He made the announcement after Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to the president earlier this week.

ARMY SECRETARY DAN DRISCOLL SUBMITS RESIGNATION TO TRUMP

Telle, who was nominated by Trump and confirmed by the Senate in 2025, oversees the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Civil Works program, where his responsibilities include flood and storm protection, commercial waterways and Clean Water Act permitting.

Previously, Telle served as chief of staff to Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., and was Trump's chief liaison to the Senate during the president's first administration, when he led the White House Office of Legislative Affairs' Senate team.

Before that, Telle served on the Senate Appropriations Committee subcommittee responsible for overseeing the Department of Homeland Security's budget. He also spent 10 years in the office of former Sen. Thad Cochran, R-Miss., where he served as deputy chief of staff, legislative director and the senator's top national security staffer.

TRUMP’S ARMY SECRETARY HUNT TAKES SHAPE AS INSIDERS FLOAT POTENTIAL PICKS

Telle is viewed as having strong relationships with senators on Capitol Hill, which could prove important as the administration works to confirm Army nominees stalled in the Senate.

The appointment fills a key leadership vacancy atop the nation's largest military branch.

Driscoll's exit came after he reportedly butted heads with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth over the Army's transformation and readiness, including Driscoll's belief that Hegseth had hindered those efforts, Fox News Digital previously reported.

US ARMY OFFERING DEFENSE FIRMS 'CONCIERGE ACCESS' TO TEST WEAPONS AT MILITARY RANGES

The outgoing Army secretary said Wednesday would be his "last full day" in the position, adding that serving under Trump and Hegseth had been "the honor of a lifetime."

"I had the privilege of working with them to modernize and accelerate how the Army mans, trains, and equips the most lethal fighting force on the face of the earth," Driscoll said in a statement posted on X.

"We could not have made the progress we did without the support of Secretary Hegseth," he continued. "I am forever grateful to President Trump for the opportunity to once again serve my country."

Fox News Digital's Ashley J. DiMella and Fox News' Jennifer Griffin contributed to this report.

item.title: Popular pantry staple could get you stopped at airport security under little-known TSA rule
item.description: The TSA has reminded travelers that peanut butter is classified a liquid under carry-on rules at airports, sparking online debate over the popular food spread.
item.content:encoded:
Travelers may want to take a second look at what they're packing for their next flight after the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) reminded passengers that one common food item is subject to its liquids rule.

The TSA recently took to X to remind travelers that, yes, peanut butter is considered a liquid when going through airport security.

"Peanut butter is a liquid... we said what we said... this time with receipts," the agency wrote.

THE BIGGEST FOOD AND DRINK MISTAKES TRAVELERS MAKE ON FLIGHTS, EXPERTS WARN

The TSA included a screenshot of a Google AI Overview explaining why peanut butter can be classified a liquid.

Under TSA rules, liquids, gels and aerosols in carry-on bags must be in containers of 3.4 ounces or fewer and fit inside a quart-sized bag, according to the TSA website. 

Larger quantities can be packed in checked luggage.

Gary Leff, a Texas-based travel industry expert and author of the blog "View From the Wing," told Fox News Digital the consistency of peanut butter is what puts it under the liquids rule.

"You can't bring peanut butter, [as] the TSA considers that to be a liquid because it conforms to the shape of its container rather than retaining its shape on its own," Leff said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

That doesn't mean travelers have to stop bringing food through security altogether.

"There are more things you can bring through security than you might even realize," Leff said.

He suggested travelers consider eating before heading to the airport or try packing foods that are allowed through security, particularly because airport dining can be expensive and options may be limited.

"Wherever you go that's not the airport is going to have better food at the same price," Leff said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the TSA for comment.

The TSA's classification has sparked debate among travelers online, with some questioning whether the popular spread should really count as a liquid.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"I would invite TSA to drink a pint of peanut butter, then," one Reddit user joked.

"So make your sandwich first," another commenter said, offering a simple workaround for travelers hoping to bring the spread along.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Fox News Digital previously reported on another TSA reminder that sparked debate among travelers after the agency weighed in on an unusual airport practice.

In July, the TSA suggested travelers could bring hammocks to airports during long layovers, writing on social media, "Nobody said you couldn't bring a hammock to the airport."

The agency advised travelers to check with individual airports before setting up a hammock because rules about where they can be used vary by airport.

The suggestion divided travelers online. 

Some said hammocks are disruptive in crowded terminals, while others embraced the idea as a way to get comfortable during long waits.

item.title: Excavation set to begin on Trump administration's 250-foot triumphal arch amid legal battle
item.description: Doug Burgum announced the start of excavation on the 250-foot Great Triumphal Arch in Washington, D.C., but a lawsuit challenges the project's authorization.
item.content:encoded:
Excavation work will begin over the next two weeks on a site where the Trump administration plans to build a tall memorial arch in Washington, D.C., a project that faces a lawsuit from opponents who argue the project will disrupt nearby historic sight lines.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum announced Thursday that work would start on the Great Triumphal Arch and Military Observation Deck, which will be located on Columbia Island, standing between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

"This will be one of the Great Pieces of American Architecture, honoring the history and significance of Arlington Cemetery and befitting the most powerful Capital in the World," Burgum wrote on X, along with mock-ups of the towering 250-foot arch.

LEAVITT SHOWS OFF US TRIUMPHAL ARCH, WITH PLANS TO BE RELEASED THURSDAY

The images showed a white arch with gold detail, with "ONE NATION UNDER GOD" written on top. A gold Lady Liberty-like figure with wings and a torch stands above, as well as gold eagles with their wings spread outward.

The project faces opposition from three veterans and an architectural historian who argued that "congressional authorization is necessary and lacking for this project," said Nicolas Sansone, an attorney with the Public Citizen Litigation Group representing the plaintiffs.

WHITE HOUSE TOUTS TRUMP’S ‘BOLD VISION’ FOR TOWERING INDEPENDENCE ARCH FOR AMERICA 250

"We believe that construction cannot and should not proceed apace, and we are prepared to inform the court that it needs to, at this juncture, step in," Sansone told The Associated Press.

A 24-page report released last month by the National Park Service backs the idea for the arch.

However, the report noted that the project would have "direct and indirect adverse effects on the sight lines of historic properties."

TRUMP'S PLAN FOR TRIUMPHAL ARCH MOVES STEP CLOSER TO REALITY

In a series of posts on X, Burgum defended the project, saying the idea for a monument goes back decades. He cited attempts by past Congresses and old reports about discussions of the construction of a memorial.

The secretary noted that more than 70 cities, including Athens, London, Madrid, New Delhi, Paris and Rome showcase arches.

"Interestingly, Washington, DC, is the only major Western capital without an arch," Burgum wrote. "Now after 125 years of waiting, the most powerful capital in the world will be the home of the most spectacular and beautiful arch of them all!"

TRUMP’S DC BEAUTIFICATION PUSH WINS RARE DEM PRAISE AS PRESIDENT SNAPS LANDMARKS BACK TO LIFE

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Interior Department and the Public Citizen Litigation Group.

The arch is one of several projects undertaken by the Trump administration, including the renaming of the Kennedy Center, a new White House ballroom and the refurbishing of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: GOP candidate gets busted allegedly trying to plant drugs on his political rival
item.description: Thomas Ross allegedly conspired to plant cocaine and Adderall in his Republican rival's purse, but his campaign manager wore a wire for the FBI.
item.content:encoded:
A Republican candidate for the Missouri state House is facing federal drug charges after newly unsealed court documents revealed an alleged plot to frame his political opponent by planting cocaine and prescription pills in her purse.

Thomas Christopher Ross, 37, made his initial court appearance Thursday in U.S. District Court for the Western District of Missouri in Springfield, where he faced one count of conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance. 

According to the Justice Department (DOJ), Ross conspired with his former campaign manager to stash narcotics among the personal property of his Republican rival, Louise Secker, ahead of the state's August primary.

But, according to an unsealed FBI affidavit, the campaign manager reportedly flipped on Ross and wore a wire to catch him in a sting operation.

VULNERABLE DEM'S OWN AUDIT ADMITS MEDICAID OVERSIGHT FAILURE AMID MASSIVE STATEWIDE FRAUD SCANDAL

"The circumstances of his arrest are serious and deeply troubling," said Peter Kinder, chairman of the Missouri Republican Party, after news of Ross's arrest. 

"Being the Republican nominee for public office carries with it a responsibility to the voters, the community and the principles our party represents. ... Given the seriousness of the situation, I believe the right course of action is clear."

Kinder called on Ross to drop out of the race after he just narrowly won the Republican nomination for Missouri's state House of Representatives District 161 earlier this month by just a handful of votes against Secker to advance to the November general election against Democrat Aaron Metzger. Under Missouri election law, Ross has until Sept. 8 to voluntarily withdraw his name from the November general election ballot.

DON'T LET FAKE ELECTION WEBSITES FOOL YOU BEFORE 2026 MIDTERMS

"The American people deserve confidence in an electoral process that has served our nation for generations," Matthew Price, U.S. attorney for the Western District of Missouri, said in a Justice Department press release published Thursday.

"Candidates are expected to conduct their campaigns with integrity, honesty and respect for their opponents, allowing voters to make informed decisions without fear of misinformation or undue influence."

The DOJ said it was contacted July 30 by the Joplin Police Department (JPD) regarding claims of public corruption after Ross' campaign manager told JPD about the conspiracy to plant cocaine and an Adderall pill, both Schedule II narcotics, among Secker's belongings. 

The staffer said he was asked by Ross to plant a baggie of cocaine and a prescription amphetamine pill, both given to him by Ross, inside Secker's purse or car. The Justice Department added that the drugs were meant to be planted while Ross was out of town.

MAN ACCUSED OF USING FAKE CHIEF JUSTICE ROBERTS SIGNATURE TO GET OWN CRIMINAL CASE DISMISSED

According to a probable cause affidavit, the following day, July 31, the campaign staffer wore a wire during an encounter at Ross' home, KOLR-TV reported.

The outlet said court records showed how the campaign manager told Ross he still had "the bag and addies" and asked whether Ross still wanted the drugs planted on his opponent.

Ross reportedly responded in the affirmative, according to court documents, and the pair also sent numerous text messages discussing the conspiracy that Ross suggested "would be extreme egg on the face" of Secker.

Screenshots of text messages suggest Ross and the former campaign manager discussed the plot as early as May 31, local outlet KCUR-FM of Kansas City added.

Fox News Digital reached out to Ross for comment but did not hear back in time for publication.

item.title: Jennifer Aniston, boyfriend Jim Curtis’ chemistry shines as she reveals ‘deep fear’ during interview
item.description: Jennifer Aniston interviewed boyfriend Jim Curtis about "The Book of Possibility" at the 92nd Street Y, revealing a deep fear of public speaking.
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Aniston and boyfriend Jim Curtis’ chemistry was on full display Wednesday evening when the "Friends" star interviewed the wellness coach about his new book.

While the 57-year-old kept it professional as she questioned him about his life and how he came to write his self-help guide, "The Book of Possibility," their connection was undeniable.

The "Friends" star later revealed that she was overcoming a "very deep, deep fear of public speaking" by interviewing him.

"You’d never know it," Curtis told her.

'FRIENDS' STARS JENNIFER ANISTON AND COURTENEY COX SOAK UP THE SUN DURING MALLORCA YACHT GETAWAY

The actress started out the 30-minute interview by reminiscing about how she used to go to gym class in the building where they were sitting, the 92nd Street Y in New York City, and play dodgeball, which wasn’t her favorite thing, since she wasn’t "sporty."

"So, it was me just knowing that I was going to go into — it was dodgeball, the huge red balls — and I’d just walk into the room, and there’s no, like, yard. It’s a building, so you just have to run for dear life, cover for dear life. Stand as far back into a corner as you possibly can. So, it’s quite a full-circle moment to be back here with you, speaking of dodging balls."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

She continued to laughter, "So, I’m so excited to be here talking about ‘The Book of Possibility.’ Have I completely embarrassed you?"

"No, not yet. We’re still on track here," he laughed. "First question, please."

5 WAYS TO STAY FIT AND HEALTHY WHILE NAVIGATING MAJOR LIFE CHANGES: 'REALLY POWERFUL'

Aniston prefaced her first question by saying, "I know a lot about you," then asked the transformational coach about his journey to becoming the person he is now.

While discussing his earlier work on Wall Street carrying boxes around the New York Stock Exchange, Curtis said he began to feel accepted by the coworkers who would tease him by yelling "Run, Forrest, Run!" a reference to "Forrest Gump."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"It was the first time that I ever felt really accepted, because if they were making fun of me, I was truly accepted."

"Really?" she asked.

"Yes, please don’t adopt that," he replied. 

BRAT PACK ICON ANDREW MCCARTHY SAYS DRINKING 'DERAILED MY CAREER ENTIRELY'

Later, Curtis became emotional while discussing his "ultimate low" when he was in a hospital in severe pain struggling to get a diagnosis that made him realize "it’s time to change." Aniston also became emotional and teared up.

"What a beautiful story," she said, having to clear her throat. "Thank you so much for sharing that. And, also, you reached this point where you’re met with two roads, and you definitely went with the road less traveled in your case."

At the end of the interview, Curtis praised Aniston for her "fantastic" questions, adding that they "kind of" went over them before but not too much.

"I didn’t ask you one question that was prepared," the actress deadpanned. "I don’t know what you’re talking about."

JUST 5 MINUTES OF PRAYER COULD HAVE SURPRISING HEALTH BENEFITS, STUDY FINDS

After the interview, Curtis surprised Aniston by springing some questions on her from the audience. 

"Just relax, these won’t be very painful," he teased.

Once Aniston answered the questions about the possibilities she’s choosing, her best advice and how she handles stress — "Deep breaths and meditation" — the couple stood and hugged and shared a chaste kiss.

JENNIFER ANISTON REACTS TO EX-HUSBAND JUSTIN THEROUX'S BABY ANNOUNCEMENT

After Aniston left the stage, Curtis urged the audience to take "reckless abandon" and cheer for her as loudly as they could so she would consider taking part in another event.

The couple, who have been linked for over a year now, often keep their relationship private, although they have opened up about it in the past.

And the star shared a recent photo dump on Instagram of her summer that included a photo of her blowing a kiss to the camera with Curtis in the background.

item.title: Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell reveals how booze helped fuel his legendary 71-point game
item.description: Donovan Mitchell revealed on the "Cousins" podcast that a few New Year's drinks preceded his historic 71-point game against the Chicago Bulls.
item.content:encoded:
There are certain sports where I think it’s widely believed, if not accepted as a cold, hard fact, that alcohol can improve performance.

Hasn't everyone's golf game improved with a little swing oil?

However, I didn't think basketball was one of the sports, at least not until Cleveland Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell revealed that he dropped a cool 71 points back in 2023 with a little help from grandpa's old cough medicine.

AMERICAN TENNIS STAR AMANDA ANISIMOVA LEAVES FANS CONVINCED SHE DRANK BEER MID-MATCH WITH MYSTERY BEVERAGE

Back on January 2, 2023, Mitchell and the Cavs took on the Chicago Bulls.

The two teams ended up in an overtime thriller that the Cavs won 145-134, with Mitchell dropping a career-high 71 in the process.

"We played them on New Year’s Eve," Mitchell recalled on the "Cousins" podcast hosted by NBA greats Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady. "Then we had New Year’s in Cleveland. Then we played the next day. Now I will say this. I’ve never drank before a game in my life. It was New Year’s. So I did have a drink — a few drinks — the night before the game."

NO SEX FOR 10 WEEKS? CHAMPIONSHIP TEAM'S PLAYOFF STRATEGY RAISES EYEBROWS

Hey, many a beer leaguer has done that very thing. In fact, like I said, certain sports benefit from a few pops. Bowling is one, perhaps darts.

Hell, I've always argued that part of playing cornhole well is having a beer in your hand for balance.

"Never done that in my career," Mitchell said. "Haven’t done it since. So I tell people like that was probably what, you know, allowed me to have the night I had."

Mitchell is a professional because if that had happened to most of us, we would’ve thought, "Wait, if a few drinks equal 71 points, then it only makes sense that after many drinks I could be holding up a piece of paper with '100' written on it after the game."

Of course, that's not usually how it works...

...or is it?

item.title: Indiana farm faces backlash after honoring Charlie Kirk with corn maze display
item.description: Goebel Farms in Evansville, Indiana, faced dozens of negative Google reviews after unveiling a corn maze tribute to slain activist Charlie Kirk.
item.content:encoded:
An Indiana farm's corn maze tribute to the late Charlie Kirk drew intense community backlash, prompting the farm to issue a statement defending its decision.

Goebel Farms in Evansville told KWTX it chose to honor the slain Turning Point USA founder because of his commitment to free speech.

Kirk was fatally shot during a TPUSA event at Utah Valley University Sept. 10, 2025.

ITALIAN ARTIST UNVEILS CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL STATUE HE PLANS TO FEATURE AT TIMES SQUARE

After announcing the maze's theme this year, Goebel Farms received dozens of negative Google reviews on its business page, according to WEHT. 

The farm appears to have since removed its Google listing after previously marking the business "permanently closed," according to an Evansville Reddit thread celebrating the backlash.

In a statement reported by 14News, the farm acknowledged that not everyone agreed with Kirk's politics or methods, stating its intention was to promote civil discourse rather than deepen division.

BILL MAHER TO APPEAR IN CHARLIE KIRK DOCUMENTARY, REMEMBERS LOVING HIS INTERVIEW WITH THE TPUSA LEADER

"Our intention was not to suggest that everyone should share Charlie’s beliefs or agree with every statement he made," the statement read. 

"We recognize that he was a polarizing public figure and that many people strongly disagreed with his views and methods. Charlie was killed while publicly expressing and debating his convictions. 

"In a country founded on the principles of free speech, no person should lose his or her life for participating in political discussion. People are free to challenge ideas, criticize them and reject them — but violence must never become the response to speech.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"That is central to the meaning behind our maze. Even when our disagreements are serious, we must continue talking and listening to one another. When conversation stops, division deepens, and it becomes easier to view people as enemies rather than neighbors."

Goebel Farms defended itself as a family business, "not a political organization," adding, "Our hope remains simple: that Americans can speak openly, disagree honestly and challenge one another’s ideas without hatred or violence—and that our community can continue treating its members with dignity and respect."

Tyler Robinson, 23, is accused of assassinating Kirk, the 31-year-old father of two, roughly one year ago. 

Robinson will stand trial after a Utah judge ruled Tuesday that prosecutors presented enough evidence to move forward on all seven charges against him: aggravated murder; felony discharge of a firearm causing serious bodily injury; two counts of obstruction of justice; two counts of witness tampering; and committing a violent offense in the presence of a child.

Fox News Digital has reached out to TPUSA for comment.

item.title: Will Ospreay's era as AEW champion begins, learns he'll have title defense at All Out: 'I am the standard now'
item.description: Will Ospreay declared himself "the Billy goat" on "Dynamite" before his first AEW World Championship defense was set against Jon Moxley.
item.content:encoded:
Will Ospreay found out quickly who his first All Elite Wrestling (AEW) World Championship title defense was going to be against.

The "Aerial Assassin" started AEW "Dynamite" on Wednesday with an impassioned promo, calling his All In opponent Kenny Omega "the best wrestler in the world" for the last 10 years and "still is."

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

"I think about the people that have held this belt before," he said. "Chris Jericho, ‘Hangman’ Page, Jon Moxley, Kenny Omega, Bryan Danielson, Swerve Strickland … and I have to pinch myself a little bit. These guys were once-upon-a-time my heroes. I would watch them on TV. … These guys are my heroes and now the reality is, I’m amongst all of them. I worked hard for this, mate. All my idols, they’re now my rivals.

"I’m one of these guys that struggle to be able to say that I’m the guy. I haven’t got that much confidence in me. But then I look down at this belt and you can all look at it through your screens, bruv, I am the standard now. I am the Billy goat. I am the best in the world. I am your AEW world champion. But Moxley has clearly shown he has a soft spot for Ospreay. Moxley helped Ospreay strengthen his body after he recovered from a neck injury. item.title: Stephen A Smith warns Hasan Piker will ‘contaminate’ Democrats in the midterms, ‘come back to haunt them’
item.description: Stephen A. Smith warns that Hasan Piker's growing political influence could haunt Democrats in general elections and hand Republicans a weapon.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN personality Stephen A. Smith warned Thursday that far-left streamer Hasan Piker could become a general election liability for Democrats, telling Politico host Dasha Burns during "The Conversation with Dasha Burns" that Piker's influence could hurt the party beyond its progressive base and give Republicans ammunition against candidates who embrace him.

Smith said he believed Piker’s growing political footprint would ultimately hurt Democrats.

"It's a negative because I think, over the long haul, from a general populist perspective, it's going to contaminate the electorate on the left side of the aisle," he said. "It's going to come back to haunt them."

HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS

The Republican National Committee (RNC) has already sought to turn Piker's relationship with Democratic candidates into a broader indictment of the party. RNC national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre told Fox News Digital in August that Democrats were refusing to confront Piker's influence as Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed faced scrutiny over campaigning with the streamer.

"El-Sayed is a terrorist sympathizer and an America-hating socialist," Baldassarre said. "His refusal to distance himself from Hamas-hugging radicals like Hasan Piker reaffirms his true allegiance is to terrorist groups, not America.

"Democrats' refusal to disavow this clown shows they either share his poisonous ideology or they're too cowardly to confront it."

Smith's warnings came as Piker's role in Democratic politics has become an issue in one of the country's most consequential Senate races. A recent Fox News poll of Michigan registered voters found Republican nominee Mike Rogers leading El-Sayed 51% to 47%, within the margin of sampling error. While 98% of self-described Democratic Socialists of America supporters backed El-Sayed, his support dropped to 69% among non-DSA Democrats and independents.

PIKER DEMANDS DEMOCRATS DEFEND HIM FROM ATTACKS, CLAIMS HE’S NO ‘TOXIC RADICAL FORCE'

El-Sayed previously explained directly to Smith why he has resisted pressure to disavow Piker, who has supported him and appeared alongside him during the campaign.

"What I'm saying is there are 3 million people who listen to Hasan," El-Sayed said. "I want to offer them a pathway into an electoral movement where, rather than sit outside of the electoral system, they see a pathway around the things that they agree with that he says that I agree with and a pathway that disavows the things that I disagree with. And, so, it's important."

Smith summarized El-Sayed's strategy as an effort to win over Piker's audience rather than an endorsement of the streamer personally.

"So, you're not thinking about him. You’re not thinking about him. You’re thinking about the 3 million people that support him, and you're trying to get those votes. That's what you're saying?" Smith said.
